column1: # UNGRADABLE.tsv -- arizona_tests: shipped programs that CANNOT be graded as standalone programs, each named
# with the reason MEASURED against the oracle. THE PACKAGE LOCKDOWN (Lon 2026-09-06).
# Columns: path <TAB> REASON <TAB> evidence (the oracle's own words + how it was measured).
# Paths are relative to this package root: the suite ships TWO subdirectories, so a bare basename is ambiguous.
# ORACLE: icont/iconx 9.5.25a, /home/resources/icon-master/bin. CONTRACT: upstream's own tests/general/Test-icon --
#   icont -s NAME.icn ; ./NAME (or ./NAME.exe) < NAME.dat-if-present-else-/dev/null > out 2>&1 ; diff NAME.std out
# Determinism is two runs ONE SECOND APART, never back-to-back: a back-to-back pair cannot detect clock dependence
# (env.icn passes a back-to-back check and fails a 1s-apart one -- measured 2026-09-06 by hq_I).
# ⛔ These stay IN the denominator (POPULATION LAW 2026-09-04): shipped, never graded, never counted as passed.
# ⛔ "The oracle refuses it" is NOT written where OUR OWN vendoring edit is what the oracle refuses -- those rows
#    say so and name the control (upstream's unmodified file compiles; see FINDING-2026-09-06-hq_I-...).

Not a graded test: upstream tests/general/Test-icon runs it as a BANNER (`$IC -s features.icn -x`) to report the interpreter enabled build features, and never diffs it -- which is why upstream ships no features.std. Its output enumerates the ORACLE build (co-expressions, dynamic loading, external values, keyboard functions, large integers, pipes, system function); a different implementation legitimately prints a different set, so diffing it would grade the BUILD, not the language.
